# Native Muscle Experiment Bundle

## Scope and State Authority

F07d #11908 connects the merged Tools `ExperimentReplayBundle` authority to
the existing OpenSim native muscle excitation replay kernel. It does not add
an integrator, muscle law, or acceptance evaluator. Initial admission is a
reviewed cold-start subset with Millard equilibrium muscles, fixed path
points, Slider/Pin joints, muscle forces and gravity. Constraints, locks,
clamps, moving points, contact, other forces, plugins and unreviewed concrete
components remain excluded. All excluded engines and production variants
remain in the required parity denominator.

Every named continuous state must be supplied without defaults or muscle
equilibration. Native continuous `Y` coverage is checked, but does not prove
complete SimTK State serialization. Scalar actuators allocate discrete
override force and an override modeling option; muscles also allocate
activation/tendon modeling options. Coordinate clamp options are likewise
distinct from continuous state. Registered discrete-variable and modeling-option
path/value sets are included as auxiliary bundle state, together with force
enabled/override and muscle-mode flags. Fresh initialization must reproduce
these values exactly. Unsupported private subsystem or abstract state remains
outside this policy, rather than being reported as absent or zero.

The primary native source review is
[Actuator.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Actuator.cpp),
[Muscle.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Simulation/Model/Muscle.cpp), and
[Component.cpp](https://github.com/opensim-org/opensim-core/blob/85aaf6450a2f22457dac4d1ab35adfed9d3a8e43/OpenSim/Common/Component.cpp).
The recorded binary build identifies its runtime separately; reviewing source
does not attest source-to-binary equivalence or transitive library closure.

## Input and Execution

Saved dimensionless excitation is bounded in $[0,1]$ and linearly interpolated
by the existing time-only native player. It is not muscle force or joint
torque. Activation and compliant fiber dynamics remain in the native plant.
All input times are finite, increasing simulation-relative seconds beginning
at zero. Adaptive Runge--Kutta--Merson uses the fixed policy accuracy $10^{-8}$.
A fresh model and Manager execute the full horizon without observations,
feedback callbacks, state corrections or re-equilibration after restoration.

Source bytes, loaded model XML, native runtime/build, executed adapter/kernel,
shared admission helper, native extension binaries, ordered muscle channels,
state schema, initial values and execution/input policies are bound. Bundle
serialization and required capabilities are revalidated before execution.
Provider hashing is scoped evidence, not a process sandbox or full DLL
dependency attestation. Execution requires exclusive native process ownership.

## Evidence and Remaining Gates

Commit `a8e63b4cda` records six native missing-module RED tests before the
implementation. Eight actual OpenSim4.6 tests pass, checking fresh
continuous-state reproduction, native excitation readback, explicit registered
options, missing fiber rejection, changed source rejection, and an unreviewed
force rejection. These are synthetic development fixtures only. The source-byte ownership and explicit-unit regressions also pass. Scoped
mypy, all five central gates, DRY, LoD, architecture, canonical governance and
generated-context checks pass. Additional law coverage, derivative/force
initialization audits and publication remain pending at this checkpoint.

The 520-muscle candidate has locked coordinates, couplers and non-muscle
actuators and is not admitted by this policy. Native position geometry and
marker fitting are separate from dynamics qualification. Full-body anatomy,
frame registration, physiological/passive-force feasibility, contact and grip,
training-only calibration, heldout accuracy, uninterrupted muscle-driven
capture replay and all-engine/model parity remain open.
